title: I retire next year with no children. Should I sell all my properties?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #198 | DO I SELL ALL PROPERTIES AFTER RETIREMENT?
excerpt: A single woman retiring next year owns a PJ terrace and three paid-off rented units, plus a condo under construction. Sean says set a budget for the life she wants, then sell or refinance to fund it.

qa.asker: Miss I, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: Miss I retires next year and has no children. She lives in a double-storey terrace in PJ and owns three fully paid units, a medium-cost condo and a studio in PJ and a condo in Wangsa Maju, rented out at RM1,000, RM1,300 and RM1,400. A condo in Cyberjaya, near a hospital and a nursing home, is under construction. She plans to move to Ipoh near her sister, and later into the Cyberjaya condo.
qa.question: Should she sell everything because managing the properties will get harder with age, and if so, when, since people say the market is always slow?
qa.quote: If you can actually time the market, everyone here will be a millionaire already.
qa.answer: Don't let the market decide. Work out what her retirement will cost, then choose how to fund it: hold everything for the rent, sell one unit every few years, or refinance each unit only as far as its rent can repay and keep the cash. A mix of the last two gives her both income and a lump sum.

reasons.title: Rent already pays for a comfortable life
reasons.body: The three units bring in roughly RM3,000 to RM3,700 a month with no loans. With some part-time or consulting work in Ipoh, that could make a very easy life with zero commitments.

reasons.title: Nobody knows how long the money must last
reasons.body: Spending RM15,000 a month, about RM180,000 a year, a large sale might last only about ten years with inflation. Steady cash flow handles a long life better than a pile of cash she is afraid to spend.

reasons.title: Refinancing unlocks cash faster than selling
reasons.body: Refinancing each unit only up to the amount its rent can repay could release a lump sum of maybe RM400,000 to RM500,000 while the units still pay for themselves. Selling a property takes close to a year from finding a buyer to receiving the money.

reasons.title: Sell the weakest first
reasons.body: If she sells, start with the units least likely to appreciate, the PJ studio and the Wangsa Maju condo, then the medium-cost condo, and keep the PJ terrace longest to benefit most from inflation.

actions: Write down the lifestyle she wants in retirement and what it will cost each year.
Set a target selling price for each property and sell only when the market reaches it.
Consider releasing cash by refinancing to the point where each unit's rent covers the new instalment.
Allow about a year for each sale.
Prepare a will and decide where she wants to live in her final years.
qa.caveat: Selling everything mainly buys liquidity, for example to invest in dividend stocks. Sean himself would refinance and keep buying rather than hold paid-off units, but says there is no single right way.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #198. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in January 2023; values are his rough estimates. Refinancing in retirement depends on age and income, so check with banks.
